name: Crawler running
ownerWords:
<duties>: there are some things that are obvious even now.
- Keep crawler running actively
  - Check the Observability and Metrics
  - Geonode mbps >=100mbps always
  - (when p1, p2,p4 is achieved, withinnitial stability 6h+ check, they now should come to duty.)
  - instagram profiles at 10k+/min,
  - nothing is backlogging: pg -> os/ch, media worker, (... idk you know better.)
  - ...
  - when p6 is achieved, it is your duty to keep LGTM and Grafana dashbaords up to date to any changes, and carefully tune the alerts system. if it's false alert -> try to reduce it change condition. if alert missed it (wasn't in place) but found actually meaningful issue, add that alert so we don't have to worry about it.
goal: The prod crawler keeps running, and the owner sees it on the crawler dashboards on obs.virev.ai: Instagram good profiles keep flowing, GeoNode carries at least 100 Mbps, no Instagram queue starts to grow, and every panel on the crawler dashboards draws. The profile floor is 1,000 a minute for now, the lowest hourly rate the running crawler held in the 6 h to 10-19 15:16Z (1,018 a minute, 13:16 to 14:16Z). Plan goals join this duty only after they hold: when p826 (10,000 good profiles a minute) has held 6 h, it closes and this floor becomes 10,000; when p827 (nothing in the Instagram pipeline backlogs) and p829 (every profile re-read within 14 days) have each held 6 h, each closes and its number becomes a metric here, and a later slip puts a fix step back on the plan. Until a goal has held 6 h its number stays on the plan. p829 closed into the 14-day metric here on 10-21, and p683 (every read account refreshed at least weekly) into the 7-day one. GeoNode retries, supply holds and dropped exits stay with the GeoNode proxy use duty (d2), read cost per profile with the Crawler read cost duty, and once p831 closes the Crawler alerts duty (d5) keeps the dashboards and alert rules current. The census job failure share is reported in the run detail against the owner's 40 to 70% band, and a rise past it is an alert rule's job.

metrics.label: Prod Instagram good profiles read a minute, last 30 min
metrics.why: Floor while p826 is open: the lowest hourly rate of the running crawler in the 6 h to 10-19 15:16Z was 1,018 a minute (m-profiles-rate). It becomes 10,000 when p826 holds 6 h.

metrics.label: GeoNode Mbps, last 30 min
metrics.why: The owner's words: Geonode mbps >=100mbps always (10-19).

metrics.label: Instagram queues whose backlog grew over the last 6 h
metrics.why: The owner's words: nothing is backlogging: pg -> os/ch, media worker. Kafka lag, dead letters, the search sync outbox and Redis stream lag, read like the 10-19 m-backlogs check of 38 prod series.

metrics.label: Panels on the crawler dashboards on obs.virev.ai that show an error or No data
metrics.why: The owner's words: Check the Observability and Metrics (10-19). A blank panel is a number he cannot see.

metrics.label: Read Instagram accounts last read over 7 days ago, 1% sample
metrics.why: The owner's words (10-18): all refreshed at least weekly. p683 closed into this metric on 10-21: it read 0.82% at 10-20 20:55Z, then 0.588% at 10-21 01:01Z, 0.189% at 04:09Z and 0.064% at 06:05Z. 1% is p683's done line; accounts in a failing streak and sampling noise keep a small share past 7 days.

metrics.label: Read Instagram accounts re-read within 14 days, 1% sample
metrics.why: The owner's words (10-19, p829): Every Instagram profile is re-read at least once every 2 weeks. p829 closed into this metric on 10-21 after holding 6 h past its first 14-day crossing (10-20 21:58Z): 3 of 397,538 sampled read rows (99.9992%) were past 14 days at 06:05Z, all three accounts Instagram refused 8 to 16 reads in a row. 99.99% is the line where about 4,000 accounts on prod past 14 days put a fix step back.

onMiss: For each missed metric, start or steer one live fix job this run, and keep it until the metric is met again. A live job that already owns the cause gets the numbers by message: p826's census owner for the profile rate, geonode timeouts our side for GeoNode and transport failures, instagram ingest backlog for the media and OpenSearch queues, crawler prod alerts for the dashboards. Otherwise start one with rlm.create_session and put its fix step under the matching goal with duty "<id>/<metric>". ig_profiles_per_min: find what stopped or slowed the crawl (a pause, a deploy, a hold, the gateway, a crashed role) from the dashboards and logs, and get it back with a code or config fix through the crawler ops train. geonode_mbps: find which lane lost bandwidth and why, and fix our side; never contact GeoNode (c37). ig_queues_growing_6h: name the queue and its consumer from the backlog line and fix the consumer. crawler_panels_blank: the dashboards line names each blank panel; fix its query in auto-sns-agent apps/infra/grafana/dashboards/crawler or the exporter it reads, or delete a panel nobody needs, and land it through the crawler ops train. ig_read_past_7d_pct and ig_read_within_14d_pct: the refresh line names how many sampled rows are past and how many sit in the history lane; find which rows are behind by lane, state and last_error (the history lane after a failed walk, the profile lane's backlog, a cadence control such as weekly_days, monthly_days, private_days or small_recheck_days, or a read path that keeps failing) and fix it with code or a control write through /ops/controls with a measured reason, through the instagram weekly refresh job when it is live. When p826 or p827 has held 6 h on its plan number, close it and update this duty file as its goal says, then run add.ts. A source_error comes first: fix the precheck read. The duty job itself only reads prod. All on target: end the turn with no message.
